problem: Prior ALFRED agents use a flat policy that learns navigation and object interaction jointly with shared parameters, despite their very different reasoning needs and the imbalance between frequent navigation and rare interaction actions. Strong prior agents also rely on rule-based planners, semantic maps, depth supervision or perfect egomotion.
motivation: Long-horizon household tasks are compositions of navigation and interaction subgoals. Navigation needs temporal and global context while interaction needs local visual cues and stationary views. Splitting the task into subgoals with specialised policies should make learning easier, faster and more efficient, and make behaviour interpretable, without map or planner assumptions.
key_idea: A three-level hierarchy of a policy composition controller that predicts subgoal sequences, a navigation-only master policy with an object encoding module as a stopping monitor, and separate per-subgoal interaction policies.
insight: The navigation/interaction hierarchy (NIH) and the object encoding module (OEM) give the biggest gains. Removing NIH drops val-unseen SR from 20.08 to 12.43, removing OEM drops it to 13.31, and removing modular interaction policies drops it to 15.82. The hierarchical agent also converges faster than the flat one (25 vs 37 epochs) and has shorter episodes. Knowing the target object, taken from the following interaction instruction, works as a navigation stopping criterion. The purely learned agent generalises better to unseen scenes than seen-biased flat agents, but heuristic or planner-based methods still have higher SR.
method: Policy Composition Controller (PCC): Bi-LSTM + self-attention encodes each step-by-step instruction and a single FC layer classifies it into a predefined subgoal type. It is trained by imitation and reaches 98.5% accuracy on validation, giving the interpretable subgoal sequence.

Master Policy: an LSTM navigation policy over MoveAhead/Rotate/Look actions plus a <MANIPULATE> token that hands control to an interaction policy. It takes panoramic attended visual features (VL-Ground dynamic filters), the combined navigation+next-interaction subtask instruction, the previous action and the object encoding.
Subtask language encoding: navigation subgoal T and the following interaction subgoal T+1 are concatenated, because the target object is often mentioned only in the interaction instruction.

Object Encoding Module (OEM): Bi-LSTM + 2-layer MLP predicts the target object class from the subtask instruction. At test time a pretrained Mask R-CNN checks whether that object is visible and, if so, switches to the interaction policy.

Interaction Policies: one per subgoal type, each with a separate action prediction module and an object-class-based mask module (Mask R-CNN mask), with an isolated hidden state, trained by imitation. This follows MOCA's factorisation.
Loop Escape Module: a heuristic that detects repeated observation sequences (window W=10) and takes a random navigation action. It improves PLWSR (val-unseen 7.91 to 10.84) but barely changes SR.
Training: modules are trained independently by behaviour cloning, with interaction policies converging in about 2 epochs, plus visual feature augmentation.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 visual features + Bi-LSTM/LSTM policies, Mask R-CNN (all trained from scratch/pretrained, no LLM)
setting.training_data: ALFRED expert trajectories with subgoal labels and step-by-step instructions, plus visual feature augmentation; no extra synthetic data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB plus 4 surrounding views (rotate left/right, look up/down), language goal and step-by-step instructions; no depth
setting.action_space: low-level discrete ALFRED actions (MoveAhead, Rotate, Look, Pickup, Put, Open, Close, Toggle) plus <MANIPULATE>/<STOP> control tokens and Mask R-CNN interaction masks
setting.privileged: none at test time (uses ground-truth subgoal labels only for training)

results: MCR-Agent reaches 20.08 SR / 10.84 PLWSR on val-unseen and 17.04 / 9.69 on test-unseen. It beats the comparable learned baselines (HiTUT 13.87/5.86, M-Track 16.29/7.66 on test-unseen) without planners, semantic maps or depth. It claims a 2.03% absolute PLWSR gain on unseen over comparable prior work. Map- and planner-based methods (FILM 26.49 SR, EPA 36.07 SR on test-unseen) have higher SR, but EPA and HLSM have much lower PLWSR.
limitations: SR is still well below planner- and map-based methods (FILM, EPA) and seen-unseen gaps remain large.

Separate policy networks per subgoal increase memory linearly (0.23GB each), and the pipeline depends on the predefined subgoal set, ground-truth subgoal labels for PCC training, and Mask R-CNN detection.
Behaviour cloning only, with a heuristic loop escape module and hand-designed inductive biases.
